Description: The President's Council of Advisors on Science and Technology (PCAST) is an advisory group of the Nation's leading scientists and engineers, appointed by the President to augment the science and technology advice available to him from inside the White House and from cabinet departments and other Federal agencies., The Federal Government has invested over $20 billion in nanotechnology research, leading to significant advancements. PCAST recommends transitioning towards commercialization through Grand Challenges, addressing environmental, health, and safety issues, and sustaining research infrastructure., The PCAST 2014 review assesses the progress and challenges of the National Nanotechnology Initiative, highlighting funding issues, international competition, and the transition to NNI 2.0., This report provides recommendations for the NNI 2.0, focusing on programmatic focus, program management, commercialization, measurements, and EHS concerns. It emphasizes the need for a Grand Challenges framework, an advisory committee, and metrics for assessing research and commercialization funding., The document outlines recommendations for the National Nanotechnology Initiative 2.0, focusing on Grand Challenges, program management, commercialization, and research enterprise to enhance the impact of Federal nanotechnology activities and transition to commercialization., The report conveys the fifth review of the National Nanotechnology Initiative by the President's Council of Advisors on Science and Technology, highlighting recommendations for supporting high-risk research, nanoscale research centers, and a multidisciplinary nanotechnology environmental, health, and safety ecosystem., The report reviews the Federal Government's actions and investments in nanotechnology, highlighting the coordination of activities and collaborations across agencies. It discusses the development of smart glass by Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory and nanotube-infused clothing for chemical protection., A research team at NIST has demonstrated carbon nanotubes that degrade nerve agents. The document outlines Federal activities under the National Nanotechnology Initiative and describes international competition., Federal activities in nanotechnology range from investments in foundational research to efforts aimed at enabling commercial applications of nanotechnology-enabled products and solutions. The NNCO aggregates individual agency budget requests for nanotechnology and Congressional appropriations into a comprehensive annual report to provide visibility to the overall national investment in nanotechnology., The 2014 NNI review report is organized into chapters around categories of recommendations, focusing on NNI goals, grand challenges, program management, commercialization, research enterprise, and environmental, health, and safety issues., This document outlines the proposed 2015 agency investments by program component area in dollars, along with an assessment of the NNI goals and progress in nanotechnology research and development., The document discusses the progress and challenges in achieving the goals of the National Nanotechnology Initiative (NNI), focusing on nano-enabled products, workforce development, and responsible development of nanotechnology., The document discusses the global context of nanotechnology research, commercialization, and regulation, highlighting the roles of various countries and the importance of international collaboration., The document discusses the development and challenges of nanotechnology, focusing on the transition to NNI 2.0, Grand Challenges, and Nanotechnology Signature Initiatives., The document discusses the assessment of Nanotechnology Signature Initiatives (NSIs) by the National Research Council Committee, focusing on funding, collaboration, and strategic planning. It also outlines the characteristics of Grand Challenges in nanotechnology., Recommendations for establishing and implementing Grand Challenges in nanotechnology, focusing on societal needs and manufacturing challenges., The document discusses the use of nanotechnology in desalination to address water shortages and in solid-state refrigeration to reduce greenhouse emissions. It also covers the potential of nano 3D printing in manufacturing., Development of a Nanoscale Therapeutic for at Least One Major Cancer Type by 2030. Focus on novel, multifunctional nano-carriers for cancer treatment and early detection. Challenges include late disease detection, tumor physiology, and toxicities. A 10-year horizon with early milestones in tumor targeting and biomarker detection., The report discusses the deployment of Grand Challenges to enhance leadership and management of NNI 2.0, focusing on program management and responses to previous recommendations., The document discusses the recommendations and progress related to the National Nanotechnology Initiative (NNI) and its leadership roles, budget allocations, and strategic planning. It highlights the lack of progress against 2012 recommendations and emphasizes the need for increased leadership and strategic alignment within the NNI., Recommendations for managing Federal nanotechnology activities, aligning review intervals, and involving cross-sector experts in NNI guidance., Discussion on the development of metrics for quantifying the Federal nanotechnology portfolio, the use of the NNI definition of nanotechnology, and the need for improved measurement systems to assess the impact of nanotechnology investments., Discussion on the commercialization of nanotechnology, including revenue growth, investment levels, and challenges in the sector., The document discusses the process, drivers, challenges, and stakeholders involved in moving a promising technology from research to product development in the U.S., highlighting the role of federal agencies, public-private partnerships, and consortia in commercialization., The document discusses constraints inhibiting nanotechnology commercialization in the United States, focusing on peer-review challenges, inexperience of first-time entrepreneurs, limited communication among stakeholders, and limited capital for new entrepreneurs. It highlights the need for investment in nanofabrication facilities and comprehensive nanotechnology EHS standards., Discussion on the commercialization constraints specific to nanotechnology, focusing on nanofabrication facilities and EHS standards, and the impact on U.S. competitiveness. Highlights the 'Valley of Death' in technology development and the need for infrastructure to support commercialization., The document discusses the creation of the National Network for Manufacturing Innovation (NNMI) and the NSF Innovation Corps (I-Corps) program, focusing on manufacturing innovation and entrepreneurship in nanotechnology., The document discusses the challenges in nanotechnology commercialization due to poor communication among stakeholders and suggests solutions such as partnering sessions at scientific meetings and the establishment of a 'clearing house' for nanomaterial information. It also highlights the need for robust metrics to measure the economic impact of nanotechnology., Discussion on the role of universities and state initiatives in supporting technology transfer and commercialization, particularly in nanotechnology., The chapter discusses the focus on setting up platforms for nanotechnology commercialization while supporting discovery and exploratory research. It emphasizes the importance of a balanced portfolio in discovery, exploration, and commercialization to achieve Grand Challenges. The chapter also highlights the need for major research breakthroughs in atomic scale control, active nanostructures, and integration in nanoscale assemblies., Discussion on fostering discovery by supporting talented researchers at various career stages, challenges faced by senior researchers in the U.S., and recommendations for supporting high-risk research in nanoscience and technology., Achieving Grand Challenges in nanotechnology requires transdisciplinary research. Federal agencies invest in research centers to catalyze exploration, providing infrastructure and training for future scientists. Centers face risks like high costs and potential stifling of innovation, but strong leadership and flexible goals can mitigate these. Center-based grants are crucial for training interdisciplinary scientists., Discussion on the establishment and support of nanoscale-focused research centers and infrastructure networks, including the role of various federal agencies and the importance of addressing environmental, health, and safety issues related to nanotechnology., The document reviews the 2012 PCAST recommendations on nanotechnology EHS and assesses the current status of nanotechnology EHS, highlighting the integration of research for regulatory decision making and commercialization., The document discusses the need for integrating available knowledge for safety assessment, decision analysis, and regulatory approval of nanotechnology products. It highlights the importance of addressing knowledge gaps, coordinating efforts among government, industry, and academia, and improving hazard and risk assessment through mechanistic approaches and tiered risk assessment. It also emphasizes the need for better instrumentation for exposure and dosimetry analysis and the importance of lifecycle analysis., Discussion on the need for a multidisciplinary workforce in nanotechnology EHS, ethical, legal, and societal implications of nanotechnology, and recommendations for developing a nanotechnology-EHS ecosystem., The project uses digital technologies to capture data on the scientific, social, economic, and workforce results of Federal science and technology investments. It applies new technologies like natural language processing and administrative records to analyze research activities and outcomes. The field of nanomedicine is explored for its potential to transform diagnosis and treatment of diseases., Discussion on the advancements and challenges in nanotechnology applications in medicine, including drug delivery, diagnostics, and manufacturing processes., The document provides an overview of the National Nanotechnology Initiative's strategic plan, including working groups, coordination offices, and organizational charts. It also discusses funding allocation, performance analysis, and strategic initiatives for nanotechnology-related research., The document discusses various aspects of science metrics, innovation, and the impact of federal investments in science. It includes references to the STAR METRICS partnership and its role in documenting federal investments in science., Exploration of university-industry spillovers, innovation networks, faculty patenting, university licensing, manufacturing innovation institutes, and technology transfer.

Description: An advisory report by the President's Council of Advisors on Science and Technology on combating antibiotic resistance, including policy recommendations and contributions from leading scientists and engineers., Report prepared by PCAST offering recommendations to combat antibiotic resistance., The report provides practical and actionable recommendations for the Federal Government to combat the rise of antibiotic resistance, threatening health, economic growth, and security., Improving surveillance of antibiotic-resistant bacteria, increasing longevity of current antibiotics, and developing new antibiotics. The CDC estimates significant economic impact due to antibiotic-resistant infections. Challenges include overuse in human health care, use in animal agriculture, and a failing drug development pipeline., Recommendations for Federal investments and actions to combat antibiotic resistance, including strengthening surveillance, stewardship, and development of new antibiotics., Recommendations for expanding research on antibiotics, developing alternatives in agriculture, establishing clinical trials infrastructure, creating regulatory pathways, and increasing economic incentives for antibiotic development., Recommendations for antibiotic stewardship in healthcare and animal agriculture, including CMS regulations, Federal Government funding requirements, and international coordination., The document discusses the impact of antibiotics on public health, the rise of antibiotic resistance, and the historical context of infectious diseases in the 20th century., Antibiotic resistance is a significant threat to global health, with millions affected worldwide. The CDC and WHO highlight the economic and health impacts, including resistant strains like CRE and XDR-TB., The document discusses the rising issue of antibiotic resistance, highlighting the resistance of gonorrhea to third-generation cephalosporins and the spread of resistance among common infections like fluoroquinolone-resistant E. coli. It also addresses the overuse of antibiotics in human healthcare and the need for better public health measures., The document discusses the use of antibiotics in animal agriculture, the lack of new antibiotic drug development, and the need for improved surveillance and response systems to combat antibiotic resistance., The report discusses the need for federal investment and leadership to combat antibiotic resistance, highlighting the inadequate attention and funding it has received over the past decades. It outlines the economic and health impacts of antibiotic resistance and recommends federal actions to address the crisis., Discussion on the need for increased Federal investment and coordination to combat antibiotic resistance, including recommendations for funding and leadership structure., Federal efforts to combat antibiotic resistance, establishment of interagency Task Force on Combating Antibiotic-Resistant Bacteria, systematic surveillance and rapid outbreak response, National Action Plan to combat antibiotic resistance, The document discusses the challenges and strategies related to antibiotic resistance surveillance and response, highlighting the need for improved public health infrastructure and collaboration beyond national borders., Discussion on financial support for monitoring and preventing antibiotic resistance, and the establishment of a national capability for pathogen surveillance based on genome analysis., Recommendations for establishing a national capability for pathogen surveillance integrating epidemiological information with genomic sequence and analysis, including the establishment of a national laboratory network., Discussion on the need for high-quality reference genomes for bacterial pathogens, collaboration between CDC and NIH for genome sequencing, development of computational methods and tools, creation of a publicly accessible genomic database, and initiation of microbial surveillance efforts., The document discusses the need for pilot projects leveraging existing programs like CDC's Emerging Infections Program and NARMS, the development of surveillance and testing standards, and the establishment of a national infrastructure for genomic information analysis. It also outlines recommendations for strengthening state and local public health infrastructure and establishing a national capability for pathogen surveillance., Fundamental research is critical in overcoming antibiotic resistance, focusing on new approaches to antibiotic therapies and reducing non-therapeutic antibiotic use in agriculture., Re-sensitizing bacteria to antibiotics, understanding persister states in bacteria, searching for narrow-spectrum antibiotics, targeting non-essential bacterial functions, expanding access to natural products, supporting early-stage chemistry for novel compound libraries, expanding approaches that do not rely on traditional antibiotic molecules., U.S. investment in research and development needs to be increased to address antibiotic resistance and find alternatives to antibiotics in animal agriculture. NIH, FDA, DARPA, and USDA are involved in these efforts., The Budget includes funding for multidisciplinary institutes and recommendations for expanding fundamental research on antibiotic resistance, developing alternatives to antibiotics in agriculture, and establishing national clinical trial networks for testing antibiotics., Discussion on developing clinical trials infrastructure for new antibiotics, including state-of-the-art diagnostic tests, sharing clinical and genomic data, and platform trials. The NIH and FDA plan to convene stakeholders to discuss requirements and propose a plan. The Antibacterial Resistance Leadership Group may provide a foundation for this infrastructure. The document also discusses drug approval based on clinical trials in limited patient populations and the potential 'Special Medical Use' pathway., Discussion on the need for new antibiotics and the economic challenges in their development. Highlights the necessity of private investment and public incentives to stimulate antibiotic development., Analysis of economic challenges in the development of new antibiotics, highlighting market failures and investment issues., Discussion on the GAIN Act's impact on antibiotic development and the role of BARDA in incentivizing new antibiotics through partnerships., Discussion on BARDA's antibiotic development program, funding mechanisms, and economic incentives for drug developers including 'pull' mechanisms and delinkage models., Discussion on antibiotic development incentives including partial delinkage, Antibiotic Incentive Fund, and tradable vouchers for patent extension., Discussion on economic incentives for antibiotic development, antibiotic usage fee, and stewardship programs., Discussion on the misuse of antibiotics, the importance of antibiotic stewardship, and the impact of inappropriate antibiotic use in outpatient settings, particularly for respiratory tract infections., Discussion on the implementation and impact of antibiotic stewardship programs in hospitals and long-term-care facilities, including references to various studies and surveys., Discussion on antibiotic stewardship in outpatient settings and the importance of quality measures in healthcare facilities., Discussion on antibiotic consumption evaluation in the EU, antibiotic use surveillance systems, and the need for data collection on antibiotic usage in ambulatory settings in the US., The document discusses the role of the Federal Government in leading antibiotic stewardship and the development of rapid point-of-care diagnostics to improve patient outcomes and reduce antibiotic resistance., The document discusses the need for rapid diagnostic tests to determine antibiotic resistance, particularly for respiratory tract infections and tuberculosis. It highlights the role of the Federal Government and FDA in accelerating the development and adoption of such diagnostics, and the potential use of prize incentives., The document discusses the implementation of antibiotic stewardship programs in healthcare facilities and animal agriculture, emphasizing the role of CMS and Federal Government in driving these initiatives through regulations, quality measures, and funding requirements., The document discusses the impact of antibiotic use in animal agriculture on antibiotic resistance, highlighting the spread of resistant microbes from animals to humans and the challenges in tracing the origins of resistance., Studies on antibiotic resistance in livestock and humans, transmission patterns, and the impact of agricultural antibiotic use on human health., Discussion on antibiotic resistance in livestock, FDA guidances on antibiotic use in food animals, and the role of veterinarians., Discussion on FDA's guidance for the use of antimicrobial drugs in food-producing animals and its impact on antibiotic use and stewardship in agriculture., The document discusses strategies to decrease antibiotic resistance in humans and animals, emphasizing the importance of surveillance, data collection, and international cooperation., The document discusses international efforts to address antimicrobial resistance, highlighting the role of WHO, the Global Health Security Agenda, and the Transatlantic Taskforce on Antimicrobial Resistance., Acknowledgments of individuals who contributed to the preparation of the report

Description: Addendum to the 2016 PCAST report addressing forensic feature-comparison methods and the requirement for empirical testing of subjective methods., The document discusses the PCAST report on forensic feature-comparison methods, the responses from various stakeholders, and the debate on the necessity of empirical studies for establishing validity and reliability., Discussion on the role of empirical evidence in forensic sciences and the importance of empirical testing over experience, judgment, and professional practices., Discussion on the validity and reliability of forensic methods, including black-box and white-box studies, and the evaluation of methods like latent-print and bitemark analysis., The report discusses the lack of empirical studies establishing the scientific validity of feature-comparison methods in forensic science, specifically focusing on shoeprint analysis, microscopic hair comparison, and firearms analysis., Discussion on the validity of firearms analysis studies, highlighting the issues with set-based designs and the importance of properly designed black-box studies., PCAST reviewed efforts to extend DNA analysis to complex mixtures, focusing on probabilistic genotyping and its empirical validation. A controversy in a murder case highlighted issues with PG software., Discussion on expanding the category from 'complex mixtures' to 'complex samples' in forensic science, emphasizing the need for empirical testing and validation of forensic methods, and proposing the creation of a Forensic Science Study Group.

Description: An advisory report by the President's Council of Advisors on Science and Technology on big data and privacy., A report prepared by PCAST to complement and inform the analysis of big-data implications for policy, focusing on privacy challenges and technological capabilities., The ubiquity of computing and electronic communication technologies has led to the exponential growth of data from both digital and analog sources. New capabilities to gather, analyze, disseminate, and preserve vast quantities of data raise new concerns about the nature of privacy and the means by which individual privacy might be compromised or protected., Discussion on privacy concerns related to born-digital and born-analog data, data fusion, and the limitations of anonymization and notice and consent frameworks in the context of big data., Discussion on data deletion, metadata, notice and consent, privacy protection, data analytics, and privacy policies., PCAST's study on privacy policies and technical feasibilities, recommendations for privacy protection policies and technologies., A comprehensive review of big data and privacy led by John Podesta, focusing on technological aspects and privacy concerns., The report discusses the notions of big data and individual privacy, the promise and threats of big-data collection and analysis, and the historical development of privacy rights in the United States., Discussion on the impact of technology on privacy and PCAST's recommendations., Discussion on the evolution of privacy rights and their legal interpretations, highlighting five key privacy concerns and the impact of new technologies on these rights., Discussion on privacy protection issues in civil rights, the role of government and private sector in privacy, and the evolution of privacy rights., Discussion on privacy, legal implications, and technological impacts on privacy rights., Discussion on privacy management, locational privacy, harms from big-data analytics, foreclosure of individual autonomy, and loss of anonymity., The document discusses the implications of big data on privacy, providing examples and scenarios of current and future technological applications., The document discusses various applications of data analytics and machine learning in different industries, including gaming, retail, education, and healthcare, highlighting their potential benefits and challenges., The document discusses the use of health records, genomic information, and clinical trials data to improve patient outcomes, the role of mobile devices in detecting Alzheimer's disease symptoms, and the potential of educational data to enhance learning., Discussion on privacy challenges in education and the home's special status as a sanctuary of individual privacy., Discussion on the integration of cameras and microphones in homes, the use of gesture-reading technology, and the implications for privacy and data ownership., Discussion on privacy, technology, and social norms, including scenarios involving data collection and privacy rights of tenants and landlords., Discussion on the balance of convenience, privacy, and security in Taylor's world, and the role of big data and cloud services in processing personal data., The document discusses the collection and use of digital data, including consumer-tracking data, cookies, and fingerprinting techniques. It highlights the economic importance of such data and the regulatory proposals surrounding it., Discussion on privacy concerns related to over-collection and data fusion, with examples including the Brightest Flashlight Free app and its FTC settlement., The document discusses the collection and use of analog and digital data, privacy challenges, and technological convergence in devices like cell phones and smart sensors., Discussion on the integration of born-analog and born-digital data, facial-recognition algorithms, biometric data, sentiment analysis, and the role of analytics in big data., Data mining and machine learning, limitations and challenges, data fusion and information integration, The document discusses the differentiation between data integration and data fusion, their applications in business intelligence, and the challenges and privacy concerns associated with multi-sensor data fusion. It also covers image and speech recognition technologies and their applications in urban planning, law enforcement, and surveillance., The document discusses various technologies including video summarization, geolocation, biometrics, surveillance systems, re-identification, human-activity recognition, semantic summarization, and automated speech recognition. It also covers privacy concerns related to scene-extraction technologies and the use of social-media data. Additionally, it explores the development and application of speech-recognition interfaces and social-network analysis., Social-network analysis complements analysis of conventional databases, allowing for data fusion and visualization. It aids in unique identification, criminal forensic investigations, commerce, and disease monitoring. It also includes commercial 'social listening' services for business intelligence., Big-data analytics requires not just algorithms and data, but also physical platforms where the data are stored and analyzed. Data centers are the physical locus of big data in all its forms., Specialized software technology allows data in multiple data centers to cooperate in performing data analytics tasks, providing scaling and better performance. Technologies like MapReduce, Hadoop, NoSQL, Accumulo, and the Berkeley Data Analytics Stack are discussed. The cloud is described as a set of platforms and services enabled by data centers, with security benefits and challenges., Discussion on cloud architectures supporting big-data analytics, privacy protection technologies, and the relationship between cybersecurity and privacy., Discussion on the relationship between security and privacy, challenges in codifying privacy policies, and the future of privacy and security in technology., Discussion on cryptography, encryption technology, and data protection, including public-key cryptography and its implications for privacy and security., Discussion on public-key cryptography, electronic signatures, certificates, and encryption technologies including forward secrecy., Discussion on identity-based encryption, attribute-based encryption, zero-knowledge systems, homomorphic encryption, secure multi-party computation, and differential privacy. Also covers notice and consent in consumer privacy., Discussion on notice and consent, anonymization, deletion and non-retention in the context of big data and privacy., Discussion on privacy-sensitive data, de-identification, ephemerality, transparency, data destruction, and privacy preference profiles., Discussion on privacy policies, context and use, and the importance of controlling the use of personal data rather than just its collection., Discussion on commercial privacy systems, enforcement and deterrence of privacy policies, and potential market penetration of usage-controlled system technologies., Discussion on the Consumer Privacy Bill of Rights (CPBR) and its principles, focusing on obligations for data holders and consumer empowerments, with emphasis on adapting CPBR to big data contexts., Discussion on consumer empowerments, privacy rights, and the role of government in preventing privacy breaches in the context of big data., Discussion on privacy-sensitive data, data fusion, and policy interventions in big data., Discussion on the regulation of data analyzers, privacy issues arising from data analytics, and recommendations focusing on the actual uses of big data rather than its collection and analysis., The report discusses the regulation of big data, privacy concerns, and recommendations for privacy-related technologies and policies., A 2013-2014 internal government review of privacy-focused research across Federal agencies supporting research on information technologies, suggesting about $80 million supports research with an explicit focus on enhancing privacy or addressing privacy protection ancillary to other goals., The document discusses the importance of privacy education and the role of the U.S. in leading privacy-protecting technologies. It highlights the need for privacy expertise in various sectors and the potential for privacy-enhancing technologies., PCAST is especially grateful for the rapid and comprehensive assistance provided by an ad hoc group of staff at the National Science Foundation (NSF), Computer and Information Science and Engineering Directorate. This team was led by Fen Zhao and Emily Grumbling, who were enlisted by Suzanne lacono. Drs. Zhao and Grumbling worked tirelessly to review the technical literature, elicit perspectives and feedback from a range of NSF colleagues, and iterate on descriptions of numerous technologies relevant to big data and privacy and how those technologies were evolving.

Description: A report prepared by the President's Council of Advisors on Science and Technology addressing educational reform in mathematics, science, engineering, and technology., The report provides suggestions and recommendations for further implementation of the National Education Goals and the America 2000 strategy, emphasizing the need for higher levels of scientific and technological knowledge and skill for all Americans., The report discusses the need for dramatic and sustained actions by the President and federal government to address the science and technology challenge, focusing on education and human capability development., Discussion on the importance of education in science and technology, the establishment of National Education Goals, and the need for adaptation in the education system to meet future challenges., Discussion on educational reforms to meet developmental needs, focus on science, mathematics, engineering, and technology, and the role of federal government in supporting these initiatives., Discussion on trends in post-secondary education in science, mathematics, engineering, and technology, and recommendations for federal policy to enhance education and research., The report discusses the critical role of science and technology in the 20th century success of the United States and the challenges faced in maintaining leadership in these fields in the 21st century. It emphasizes the importance of learning, including precollege education, to meet these challenges., This report discusses the importance of developing talent in science and technology, the role of teachers, the interdependency of teaching and research, and the National Education Goals related to science and mathematics., Discussion on the progress and strategies for achieving national education goals, focusing on science and mathematics education, high school completion rates, and performance outcomes., The document discusses the national debate on education reform, focusing on the process of achieving National Education Goals, setting National Education Standards, developing a national system of assessments, and using statistical measurement instruments to compare educational performance nationally and internationally., Discussion on the development of national education standards and the need for educational reforms to achieve the National Education Goals., The AMERICA 2000 strategy encourages the design and development of experimental schools, promotes parental choice and diversity in education, focuses on improving the quality of teaching faculties, enhances mathematics and science learning, and creates environments for academically talented students., Discussion on the role of the federal government in science and engineering education, emphasizing the need for reform and support at various educational levels., Discussion on the importance of excellence and equity in science and engineering education, highlighting the need for improvement in student performance in mathematics and science., International studies indicate low performance of U.S. students in mathematics and science compared to other countries. Factors include curriculum, teaching methods, low standards, and parental involvement. Changing demographics affect the talent pool for future scientists and engineers, with under-represented groups growing disproportionately., Analysis of doctoral degree trends in the U.S. from 1981 to 1991, highlighting gender and ethnic diversity in science and engineering fields., The role of family in academic performance, the impact of poverty on talent development, the need for programs to nurture talent among all students, and the importance of enriching science and mathematics experiences., Analysis of trends in student interest and achievement in mathematics, science, and engineering education, highlighting changes in high school graduation requirements, undergraduate attrition rates, and declining interest in these fields., Discussion on the quality of U.S. graduate programs, the role of foreign students, and recommendations for achieving National Education Goals, including awards for students and scientists., The New Standards Project aims to develop national standards and a performance-based examination system, focusing on mathematics, reading, and writing. It emphasizes the importance of effort in learning and aims to modernize schools to meet world-class standards. The project highlights the need for diverse educational programs and partnerships to support students with special abilities. Federal programs like the Young Scholars Program and the Javits Gifted and Talented Education Program are crucial for nurturing talent., The document discusses initiatives to enhance science education through summer laboratory schools, mentorships, collaborations, and development of high-level science materials. It emphasizes the importance of real science experiences for students and suggests federal support for graduate fellowships and loan forgiveness programs., Analysis of the supply and qualifications of elementary and secondary school teachers in mathematics and science, highlighting issues of teacher shortages and qualifications., Discussion on the reform of teacher education and conditions of practice, emphasizing the need for improved teacher preparation programs and professional autonomy., Discussion on the need for comprehensive science education standards for teachers, similar to Science for All Americans, to improve teacher preparation and professional development., Discussion on the importance of good teaching models, emphasis on pedagogy versus content, technology in education, challenges in elementary mathematics and science education, and linking teacher education reform to school reform., Discussion on the linking of university programs for teacher education to schools, co-reform efforts, and the work of the National Board for Professional Teaching Standards. Examination of undergraduate education issues, particularly in science, mathematics, and engineering., The report discusses the inadequacies of undergraduate instruction in science and mathematics and provides recommendations for improving instructional quality and accessibility in these fields., The report discusses the challenges and recommendations for improving undergraduate and graduate education in mathematics, science, engineering, and technology, emphasizing interdisciplinary approaches and the integration of teaching and research., The chapter discusses the linkage between teaching and research, emphasizing the importance of understanding the learning process in science, mathematics, engineering, and technology. It highlights the need for research on learning, particularly in engaging young minds and addressing disparities in career pursuits among different demographics., The report discusses the integration of technology in education, emphasizing the importance of direct access to scholarly materials and research participation for students. It highlights projects like Project JASON and KIDSNET that provide research experiences to students., Recommendations for improving science and technology education in the United States, focusing on systemic reform, teacher development, and partnerships across society., Recommendations to enhance education in science, mathematics, engineering, and technology, including incentives for teaching excellence and integration of research with education.

Description: A report providing recommendations to ensure continued American leadership in industries of the future, including artificial intelligence, quantum information science, advanced manufacturing, advanced communications networks, and biotechnology., Acknowledgments of contributions to PCAST and its subcommittees, including staff from the U.S. Department of Energy, OSTP, and the Science and Technology Policy Institute., Recommendations for American leadership in Industries of the Future, focusing on AI, QIS, advanced manufacturing, communications, and biotechnology. Emphasizes multi-sector engagement, new institute structures, and workforce development., The report discusses the need for multi-sector partnerships and strategies to maintain and enhance America's leadership in Industries of the Future (IotF), including AI, QIS, and advanced manufacturing. It emphasizes the importance of broadening access to STEM education and training, especially for underrepresented communities and those affected by COVID-19., Recommendations for American leadership in IotF, enhancing multi-sector engagement in research and innovation, creating new institute structures, and ensuring a qualified, diverse workforce., The United States is at a critical juncture in advancing AI to achieve further breakthroughs and maintain leadership in AI. This report offers recommendations to accelerate basic science and translational R&D, expand investment in infrastructure, partnerships, work-based learning opportunities, training, and education., AI has the potential to transform science and technology, improve healthcare, and enhance national defense. Significant investments are needed from industry, academia, and government to address research and workforce development challenges. The U.S. industry and Federal Government are making substantial investments in AI R&D., Recommendations for increasing federal investment in AI R&D by a factor of 10 over 10 years, focusing on non-defense AI research and development., The FY 2020 President's Budget for AI R&D within NIH is $202 million. NIH is setting up the Artificial Intelligence for BiomedicaL Excellence (AIBLE) program to generate new biomedically-relevant data sets amenable to ML analysis at scale. PCAST recommends increasing funding levels and strengthening partnerships to meet goals., The document discusses the need for strategic focus on AI research investments to address challenges and opportunities in scientific applications, particularly in response to COVID-19. It emphasizes partnerships between federal agencies and industry to develop AI applications at scale., Pioneer and scale novel academia-industry AI partnership models, create national AI testbeds, secure U.S. industry investment pledges, expand NSF-based programs, direct AI science mission at National Laboratories., Recommendations for fostering international collaboration in AI, attracting global talent, and establishing an AI maturity model., Recommendations for developing a maturity model for trustworthy AI, precision regulation, AI education and training, and engaging stakeholders across government, industry, and academia., Recommendations to enhance AI faculty recruitment and retention, increase investments in AI education, and advance skill development in AI and QIS., Recommendations for accelerating U.S. quantum leadership, including engaging industry in building quantum infrastructure, investing in national quantum computing user facilities, and leading the creation of a quantum internet and intranet., Recommendations to attract global talent, foster discovery-based science, provide access to quantum technologies, and create research collaborations in Quantum Information Science and Technology., Recommendations for creating foundational discovery institutes and educating a quantum-enabled workforce to advance quantum technologies and science., Recommendations for enhancing quantum science education and workforce development, fostering international R&D collaborations, and ensuring national security in quantum research., The COVID-19 HPC Consortium provides researchers access to computational infrastructure for calculations in epidemiology, bioinformatics, and molecular modeling. Quantum computing and AI are reshaping discovery by complementing classical HPC. AI models are identifying small molecules for SARS-CoV-2 and structuring data for powerful models. The convergence of Bits + Neurons + Qubits holds future potential for scientific discovery., The Accelerated Discovery Workflow aims to enhance scientific productivity through AI and quantum computing, impacting drug discovery, manufacturing, FinTech, meteorology, and logistics., The report discusses the expansion of the National Strategic Computing Initiative to ensure U.S. leadership in high-performance computing and scalable systems, integrating AI and quantum computing. It also recommends re-energizing the Materials Genome Initiative to accelerate materials discovery., The document discusses scaling investments in software engineering and computational capacity in U.S. National Laboratories to support the Accelerated Discovery mission. It proposes new models of partnerships enabled via the National Laboratories, identifying key actions and engagement across industry, academia, and government. It also recommends the formation of lotF Institutes to offer innovative frameworks for R&D partnerships., The LotF Institutes aim to leverage convergence through multi-sector partnerships, partner-favorable IP policies, and tax incentives to accelerate economic growth. They will foster cross-agency and industry partnerships, maximize research time by reducing bureaucracy, and establish world-class facilities to support the Workforce of the Future., The proposed lotF Institutes aim to develop domestic talent and attract global researchers to the U.S. for advanced degrees and employment. They will serve as inclusive environments to explore the impact and intersection of lotF, facilitating public-private partnerships and technology transfer. Recommendations include engaging partners from all sectors, complementing existing institutes, and establishing transparent IP terms., The report highlights the value of flexible IP terms in public-private partnerships for accelerating commercialization and proposes leveraging economic opportunity zones to attract investment and advance regional development., Discussion on the role of lotF Institutes in developing digital twins and enhancing U.S. manufacturing competitiveness through advanced technologies like AI/ML and additive manufacturing., This document discusses the establishment of new institutes to expand AI and ML methods for disease understanding, treatment efficacy, and biotechnology solutions. It highlights the bioeconomy's contribution to the GDP and the need for advanced R&D in generative design in manufacturing., The document discusses the administration of IotF Institutes by DOE, challenges faced by U.S. National Laboratories, and recommendations for improving operational efficiency and talent management., The report emphasizes the need to improve access to high-quality education and training programs in STEM to build the Nation's STEM capacity and lay the foundation for the Workforce of the Future. It highlights the importance of inclusion of underserved and underrepresented individuals in STEM and outlines priorities and recommendations for workforce development and training., Boards could be structured as public-private partnerships to bring Americans into STEM jobs and strengthen skills. Increasing diversity and incorporating nontechnical skills into STEM training are emphasized. Recommendations include creating industry-recognized curricula and skills-based licenses through public-private partnerships., Educational programs with industry-recognized credentials prepare students for future jobs. Certifications guide workforce reskilling and upskilling. Programs should include experiential learning and focus on underserved populations. Employers should create skills-based job codes. Description: The report focuses on the U.S. semiconductor ecosystem, highlighting the importance of semiconductors to the economy and national security, and proposing actions to strengthen the industry through the CHIPS and Science Act., Members of PCAST and Working Group on Semiconductors, The CHIPS and Science Act aims to strengthen the U.S. semiconductor ecosystem through significant funding for R&D and manufacturing, addressing global competition and fostering innovation., Establishment of NSTC as an independent legal entity, creation of a national microelectronics education and training network, investment fund for semiconductor startups, and support for scholarships and research assistantships., Recommendations for enhancing the U.S. semiconductor ecosystem, including creating a chiplet platform, funding a national research agenda, identifying grand challenges, and improving visibility into federal semiconductor investments., The document discusses the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on semiconductor demand, the decline of U.S. leadership in semiconductors, and the strategic investments by Asian countries. It highlights the need for U.S. action to maintain leadership in the semiconductor industry., The CHIPS and Science Act is a historic investment aimed at reversing the U.S.'s declining position in the global semiconductor ecosystem. It emphasizes the need for a cohesive national strategy to revitalize the U.S. semiconductor ecosystem., Recommendations for improving federal semiconductor investment efforts and measuring progress across the industry, including metrics for the NSTC and acknowledgements of contributors.

Description: This booklet explains what biodiversity is, why it is important, why it is threatened, and what can be done to conserve it., An exploration of biodiversity, species diversity, genetic diversity, and the importance of keystone and endemic species., Genetic variation is crucial for species survival. Biodiversity exists globally, with rainforests and coral reefs housing many species. Ecosystems are dynamic interactions of living and non-living components. Biodiversity provides essential goods and services, including food and medicine., The document discusses the importance of biodiversity in providing medicinal resources, fuel, timber, fiber, cultural inspiration, and ecosystem services such as pollination, air and water purification, climate modification, and drought and flood control., The document discusses the importance of plant communities in flood control, nutrient cycling, habitat provision, economic value of biodiversity, and ecosystem services valuation., Discussion on the current high rates of biodiversity loss, factors leading to biodiversity loss, and the impact of human activities on natural habitats., The text discusses the impact of habitat fragmentation and invasive species on biodiversity. It highlights how fragmentation leads to isolated species, inbreeding, and local extinction. Invasive species, introduced by humans, are a major cause of biodiversity loss and economic damage, costing the U.S. billions annually. Examples include zebra mussels and fire ants. Overuse of resources is also a concern, threatening species like bluefin tuna and mahogany., The more we consume, the more we generate waste and pollution, which threatens biodiversity and our own health. Pollution comes in many forms - oil spills, acid precipitation, toxic chemicals in fertilizers and pesticides, and urban and suburban sewage runoff, to name a few. Pollution may kill organisms outright or it may weaken them by interfering with vital processes such as mobility and reproduction. Pesticides harm wild insect pollinators, including managed honeybee populations, which can in turn reduce crop yields. Runoff seeping into rivers, lakes and coastal environments can produce negative impacts on entire aquatic ecosystems. In the United States alone, pesticides kill an estimated 75 million birds and billions of non-target insects on croplands every year. Some 140,000 people become sick because of pesticides and pesticide runoff each year. Several pesticides banned in the United States are still exported to developing countries. Of particular concern are chemicals called endocrine disrupters such as DDT, DDE and PCBs. These substances mimic or interfere with normal hormones in living organisms. Reproductive abnormalities have been found in alligators, terns, salmon and gulls exposed to high levels of chemicals from pesticides and animal hormones in their environment., The document discusses the impact of human activities on global climate change and biodiversity loss, highlighting the consequences for ecosystems, human society, and the economy. It emphasizes the vulnerability of ecosystems to climate change and the importance of conserving biodiversity., Discussion on endangered species and ecosystems in North America, including Canada, the United States, and Mexico, and actions to conserve biodiversity., The document discusses the importance of monitoring biodiversity, understanding ecosystem functions, and the role of protected areas in conserving species and natural systems. It highlights the need for increased knowledge and the establishment of biodiversity hotspots., The document discusses the importance of ecological restoration, the role of botanical gardens and zoos in conservation, environmental education, and scientific and industry collaboration for sustainable development., The document discusses sustainable living, legal measures for biodiversity protection, and efforts in North America to protect biodiversity through national parks and other public lands. It highlights the role of ecotourism and various U.S. legislation in promoting sustainable development., The document discusses the role of various organizations and systems in the conservation of biodiversity across the United States, Canada, and Mexico, highlighting the importance of protected areas and the ecological footprint concept., A guide on living a sustainable life and supporting biodiversity conservation efforts. Includes information on local and global biodiversity organizations.

Description: The memorandum discusses the Human Genome Project, British panel recommendations on embryo cloning, Monsanto's contribution to the rice genome sequencing project, and a joint NASA/European Union campaign on Arctic ozone loss., The 'ozone hole' that forms in the Antarctic every winter and early spring is well known. Scientists are also observing the Arctic to determine if an ozone hole will form there as well. During the winter of 99/00, scientists from NASA and the European Union obtained measurements of ozone and other atmospheric gases and particles in the Arctic that show losses of over 60% in the lower stratosphere, one of the worst losses ever seen in the Arctic. A star-like image of a body about 3000 degrees Fahrenheit, apparently connected to a pair of young stars by a glowing trail, appears on an infrared picture taken with the Hubble space telescope on August 4, 1997. NASA is calling it a possible 'planet', formed at the same time as the two stars, but shot out into space about 1000 years ago by the chaotic gravity of the two stars. Assuming it formed at the same time as the two stars, whose age is calculated from standard theory, astronomers infer the 'planet' is about 1000 times more massive than the Earth. It is supposed to be glowing, not from thermonuclear energy like a star, but from the remnant of the collision energy of the dust from which it formed. Description: Interview with Luis Proenza conducted by Kenneth M. Evans and David J. Caruso via Zoom on 16 July and 6 August 2021, part of a research project on the President's Council of Advisors on Science and Technology (PCAST)., Oral history interview with Luis Proenza conducted via Zoom on 16 July and 6 August 2021, discussing his professional experiences and contributions to science and technology policy., Luis Proenza was born in 1944 in Mexico City, Mexico. He grew up in Cuernavaca and Acapulco, Mexico. He moved to Georgia to attend Riverside Military Academy and later attended Emory University. He worked with Dr. Bonnie R. Strickland and was accepted at Ohio State University. He taught at the University of the Americas before returning to the United States., Interview discussing Proenza's career, his roles in various universities, his involvement with PCAST, and his contributions to science policy., The Center for Oral History and Rice University's Baker Institute for Public Policy are committed to preserving and enhancing research use of oral history interviews by preparing edited transcripts. The process includes review and editing by staff and interviewees, with guidelines to maintain fidelity to the language and meaning of each interview.
